# Explorer service variables

The Paxeer X explorer service in `services/explorer` contains the Blockscout Elixir backend, the Rust signature provider and smart-contract verifier, and deployment scripts. It indexes the single Paxeer mainnet-beta BFT network with EVM chain id 125; the kernel runs in the node and a receipt is final when its block is committed. The deployment also passes a frontend environment file to `apps/explorer`.

Environment names and configuration keys are listed below in name order. A configuration entry names its file, section and leaf key. Elixir application settings are loaded from the named `.exs` file; development and client-specific files apply only in that mode. Runtime configuration overrides compile-time defaults. For the merged network, select `paxeer_x` for `CHAIN_TYPE` and `ETHEREUM_JSONRPC_VARIANT`; their generic source defaults remain listed.

The Rust services optionally load the file named by `SIG_PROVIDER__CONFIG` or `SMART_CONTRACT_VERIFIER__CONFIG`, then apply environment overrides. Each TOML section/key maps to an uppercase environment name separated by `__`. The listed defaults come from the settings types unless a supplied file overrides them. Compiler directories follow the system temporary directory. S3 and list fetchers are alternatives; select one fetcher for each compiler family.

The examples list deployment inputs in `services/explorer/.env.example`, backend inputs in `deploy/env/backend.example.env`, frontend inputs in `deploy/env/frontend.example.env`, signature-provider inputs in `services/sig-provider/.env.example`, and verifier inputs in `services/smart-contract-verifier/smart-contract-verifier-server/config/base.env`. They leave secrets empty. Optional inputs without a literal default are commented so that they stay unset. Endpoint and account defaults are described without publishing their values. The backend and frontend deployment examples retain the local Compose defaults supplied by those files; their generic application defaults are listed alongside them. Other inputs show literal defaults from their readers. Commented values preserve computed defaults and optional integrations.

## Required

A row states the deployment mode or enabled feature that makes the input required. Alternative database fields and endpoint lists can supply the same connection. Requirements for an optional configuration file apply only when that file or entry is supplied.

## Optional

These inputs have source defaults, are managed by the build tool, or apply to optional integrations. Names containing `<TAG>`, `<PLATFORM>` or `<ENV>` describe dynamic families; substitute the configured label, platform or deployment environment. Browser `NEXT_PUBLIC_` values are public. An unset receipt authority supplies no trust anchors, and an unset price-feed retention period retains all submissions.

| Name or file, section and key | What it sets | Source default | Secret | Source reader |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ACCOUNT_AUTH0_APPLICATION_ID` | Sets account auth0 application id | Unset | No | [services/explorer/backend/config/runtime.exs](../../../services/explorer/backend/config/runtime.exs) |
